Q1: Zirconyl chloride octahydrate has a Tier 1 classification for dermal and eye hazards (SKN1), indicating internationally recognized, significant hazards in this area based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). For most other categories, including Carcinogenicity, Mutagenicity, and Reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation hazards (IHL), oral hazards (ORL), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), the chemical is Tier 4 (data deficient), meaning insufficient information is available for confident hazard assessment.
Q2: Zirconyl chloride octahydrate does not appear on commonly recognized "Lists of Concern." This absence, combined with its many Tier 4 (data deficient) classifications across various hazard categories, suggests a potential lack of comprehensive study on its broader hazard profile.
Q3: Zirconyl chloride octahydrate is structurally well-defined, possessing a specific molecular formula (Cl2OZr.8H2O) and not classified as an Incompletely Defined Substance (UVCB). With 2701 literature references, significantly above the median for characterized chemicals, it is extensively studied in scientific literature. However, despite its structural characterization and the volume of research, its hazard profile remains largely incomplete, as six out of seven hazard classes are designated Tier 4 (data deficient).
